recent_posts.title: With Gratitude We Say Goodbye: Sunsetting Begin — Begin Blog
recent_posts.summary: The Begin team is joining forces with Sanity to create the world's first Content Operating System. Beginning January 1, 2025, Begin customer applications will be deactivated. However, customers can migrate their apps to AWS using OpenJS Architect. Architect, used by Begin Deploy, offers stable, easy-to-write IaC and works with various backend environments. Enhance users can continue to run their apps on any backend thanks to WASM. The post expresses gratitude to the team's members, investors, and customers.

recent_posts.title: Block the Bots in Enhance Projects — Begin Blog
recent_posts.summary: A new plugin called @enhance/arc-plugin-block-bots has been introduced for Enhance applications to block AI bots using a customizable `robots.txt` file. This plugin adds a `/robots.txt` route to your application to specify which user agents are disallowed from accessing your site. The plugin automatically updates the `robots.txt` file daily by checking a maintained list of AI bots. Future updates may include better bot control using middleware or Amazon WAF.

recent_posts.summary: Brian discusses the evolution and rise of serverless full stack development with Noel Minchow on PodRocket, covering the history and future of JavaScript, benefits of serverless architecture, and ways front-end developers can build scalable and maintainable applications using these technologies.

recent_posts.title: Island Architecture with Web Components — Begin Blog
recent_posts.summary: Island Architecture divides web pages into smaller, independently upgradeable units (islands), combining server-side rendering for static content and client-side interactivity for dynamic regions. Using web components fits this architecture well due to their encapsulation, reusability, and performance benefits, including improved SEO and accessibility. Enhance framework leverages this by rendering pages as static HTML and progressively hydrating interactive components, ensuring quick load times and a seamless user experience.

recent_posts.title: WebAuthn: Enhancing Security with Minimal Effort — Begin Blog
recent_posts.summary: WebAuthn is a robust, passwordless authentication API built into all major browsers, based on the W3C/FIDO2 specification. It leverages public-key cryptography to enhance security and improve user experience through methods like fingerprint sensors and facial recognition. Passkeys, a software-based implementation of WebAuthn, can sync across devices from providers like Apple, Google, and Microsoft. Implementing WebAuthn is relatively straightforward with the help of libraries like SimpleWebAuthn. Despite its many benefits, considerations include user adoption, device compatibility, account recovery, privacy concerns, and implementation complexity.

recent_posts.title: OS Selector for Documentation Sites — Begin Blog
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the importance of having an OS selector in documentation sites to provide command line instructions tailored to the user's operating system. It provides a detailed guide on building such a component using the Enhance library, including persisting OS preferences with localStorage and updating all instances of the component on the page. A shadow DOM version is also discussed.

recent_posts.title: Component Communication in Enhance — Begin Blog
recent_posts.summary: Enhance simplifies building web applications with components that encapsulate their own UI and functionality. This post explains the different ways components can communicate: from using Events for child-to-parent communication to setting attributes for parent-to-child communication. It also introduces @enhance/store, a singleton reactive data store, for managing shared state across components. Example code snippets illustrate how to implement these communication methods.
